output.brief:
The rise in missed appointments at Corrie Lane is real, and it comes from the Tidewell change. It isn't a counting problem, the bus cut, or the front desk.

- Eastgate is still on the old system and shows no rise (about 8%). Both sites share the route 14 bus, so the bus doesn't explain it. Corrie Lane's rate in the same months a year earlier was also about 8%, so seasonal variation doesn't explain it either.
- An audit of records coded as missed found that miscoding accounts for only about 0.5 percentage points.
- Phone records show the day-before confirmation calls continued at about 91–93% coverage. Those calls were only ever for the minor-procedures list. Disciplining staff would punish the wrong people.
- Two Tidewell settings changed together on the same day in every clinic: the last reminder moved from 2 days to 7 days before, and booking lead time grew from about 19 to about 52 days. The data can't separate the two. Lead-time-by-outcome data isn't available, and the vendor quotes 10 weeks for it.

I'm confident about what the cause isn't. I'm not sure which Tidewell setting matters more, or whether both do.

Next step: run the randomised 8-week test, with the 48-hour reminder on half the session templates. The vendor can change the offset within two working days. Keep reporting the rate to the board, and note the caveats. Don't change the booking horizon yet.
